experiment.goal: Spec20.2 actual inquiry, repeated inquiry and matched ReAct performance comparisons
experiment.scope: Unchanged inquiry cases --comparison-only (four paired tasks plus existing ReAct negatives), four-task repeated inquiry, and full repair application fixture. BPI2/BPC1/BPI3.
experiment.method: Instrument exact original fixture invoke intervals around fresh guest creation/admission/invocation/outcome decoding. Keep native/Wasmtime/graph and semantic assertions intact; report cumulative guest-call time separately from diagnostic total harness time. Whole-harness times include auxiliary validation and are not user latency.
experiment.sampling: First qualify every lane/format. Then three rotated process observations per format/lane in each of two windows; preserve all samples, first-call and expected-error timing separately. No paid models; actual fixture-confined qualified executor remains active.
experiment.preservation: Model/experiment/approval/write/cleanup counts, input policies, semantic summaries and expected results must agree across formats. Compare portable size and native requested working/copy counters separately; native transition counts may differ.
experiment.guard: No interpretation of timing unless all original assertions pass and semantic comparison agrees. Do not silently skip a slow/error lane.

method.timed: Each original fresh guest block: owned kernel admission/creation, complete image/State invocation, outcome production and public decoding. Expected failures are included and labelled.
method.notTimed: Native replay, Wasmtime replay, graph inspection, provider fixture construction, sandbox execution, and delivery are outside the guest interval. Their assertions remain active.
method.diagnostic: Per-process and scenario clocks include auxiliary verification and must not be called end-to-end user latency. Scenario clocks start after fixture setup.
method.sampleUnit: Cumulative fresh guest milliseconds per complete fixture scenario. Three rotated process observations in each of two windows; not request p99.
method.memoryScope: Native --statistics requested-payload peak for Session preparation/restore/execution. Input-file decoding and host/output buffers are outside that workspace; this is neither total process RSS nor total WebAssembly memory.
method.comparability: BPI2/BPC1 retain the same old Program identity. Current task/outcome schemas match predecessor bytes. The same qualified executor, task contract and fixture programs are used; inquiry.mjs differs only in its BPI2/BPI3 comment.
method.policy: Original assertions and prescribed policies remain. Semantic/work-count projection matches every measured run to qualification. Graph sizes and interpreter transitions are representation-specific and reported separately.

summary.unit: Cumulative fresh guest invocation milliseconds per complete fixture scenario, not per-request tail latency or whole-application latency.

observations.method: Three rotating processes per lane/format/window, two windows. All original native/Wasmtime/graph/semantic assertions remain. Only fresh guest intervals are performance-qualified; process and diagnostic scenario clocks include verification overhead.

clockCorrection.cause: Predecessor repeated fixture invokes three stale responses directly outside invoke; successor invokes them through invoke.
clockCorrection.correction: Time the same existing direct calls without changing their input or rejection assertions.
clockCorrection.scope: Qualification only; acceptance measurements had not started.

reproduction.inputs: Archive the exact Agent revisions in experiment.inputs into before/after. Supply the corresponding authenticated immutable Boundary/World sources and World runtimes through inputs.json. Build each original native.zig and multi_probe.zig with build-tools.zig; re-emit predecessor inquiry images/schemas through its public inquiry-application-images target. Identity-verified BPC1 uses the predecessor compact encoder.
reproduction.notes: Scripts expect a fresh absolute experiment root. Replace captured root/input paths with the new immutable inputs; retain assertion anchors and require semantic qualification before timing. No source inputs or production policies are rewritten.

results.inquiry: Main repair cumulative guest medians458.05/439.09ms versus BPC1 688.87/709.15ms; paired inquiry cases improve33-42%.
results.repeated: Four tasks including stale challenges:1157.56/1118.39ms versus2038.45/2035.16ms BPC1; same55 attempts including3 expected failures,28 models,4 experiments and8 cleanups. Quiescent States174bytes versus170; bounded within each format.
results.react: Paired reset ReAct235.83/252.75ms versus214.78/205.10ms BPC1. Rebinding and other ReAct cases also regress; all rows and ranges retained.
results.memory: Paired reset inquiry native Session peak3209470 versus1853961bytes BPC1. Paired reset ReAct5373182 versus2061220bytes. Blob-copy work falls but does not discharge these peak regressions.
results.acceptance: Incomplete: measured actual inquiry gains coexist with material ReAct latency and native working-peak failures. No strategy, model work, assertions, or denominator was reduced to obtain gains.

catalogDiagnostic.method: Admit BPI3, traverse typed catalog references from entry/result/failure using the existing relocation Mapper with a read-only reference observer. Include resource authority functions, schemas, captures and constructor references. This is a conservative typed dependency traversal, not evaluation or a production transformation.
catalogDiagnostic.finding: ReAct contains18 unused functions,22 unused schemas,2 unused effects and1 unused handler. Reachable67 functions/145 schemas/0 handlers match predecessor totals. The current closed compiler owns dense region names but retains other catalogs. Inquiry retains all109 functions, so its peak regression needs additional explanation.
catalogDiagnostic.limitation: No core code changed and no pruning performance gain is claimed. Any repair must preserve nominal/resource references and component interfaces and reject invalid input before transformation.
